uncited: *   **Input:** A ray, a set of valid Gaussians intersected by the ray ($N^{\text{val}}$), and a termination threshold $\epsilon$.
*   **Valid Gaussians:** A list of Gaussians intersected by the ray.
In cell-based variants, these are grouped by cell.
Iterate through the valid Gaussians (or cells) in front-to-back order.
Compute the contribution of the Gaussian to the color.
Update the accumulated color: $C \leftarrow C + \text{contribution}_i \times T$.
Update the transmittance: $T \leftarrow T \times (1 - \alpha_i)$, where $\alpha_i$ is the opacity.
In Cell-Based ET, compute cell-level transmittance $T_{cell}^n$.
If $T_{cell}^n < \epsilon$, halt blending for that cell and proceed to the next cell or terminate if no more cells are relevant.
*   **Order Independence:** In sort-free methods, the lack of strict front-to-back ordering can affect the accuracy of transmittance decay.
*   **Limitations:** The efficiency of cell search rasterization is contingent upon the degree of coherence between the visible regions of a cell and its associated Gaussians.
